intent: Approve a commit without a change check when only wording changed.

edit.summary:
I changed the skill so a person can approve a commit marked as wording-only without running the change check. I haven't run or tested any of it.

In `SKILL.md`:
- **Commit object:** I added an optional `wording_only` boolean property.
- **`approve_commit`:** the `checks-pass` precondition now also passes when `target.wording_only == true`.
- **`record_approval` and the `approved-commits-passed-their-checks` invariant:** I relaxed both the same way. Otherwise they would have rejected the approval the new rule allows.
- **Glossary:** the "change check" entry now mentions the exception.

In `EXAMPLES.md`, I added a scenario, `a-wording-only-commit-is-approved-without-a-check`.

Nothing in the skill sets `wording_only` on a commit, so as written, whoever creates the commit can set the flag. The request didn't say who should set it, so I didn't add an action for that.

findings.problem: The new precondition and invariant let wording_only override a failed check. A commit whose change check ran and returned checks_passed == false is still approvable and recordable as approved if wording_only is true. That contradicts the rule that a failing check blocks approval. The bypass should apply only when the check has not been run (checks_passed unset), or it should never override an explicit failure.

Nothing can set Commit.wording_only. record_commit takes no such param, commit_draft passes none, and no other action writes it. In the real flow the flag is never true, so the bypass cannot happen; the example only works because its fixture presets the flag. If it is instead set from an unverified claim, a commit gets past the whole change check (structure, semantics, scenarios, harness, past actions, stranded objects) with no way to confirm the change is wording-only. A wording edit can still change behaviour or strand objects.

The glossary and purpose still say every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed. The Authoring purpose announcement says exactly that. Other text says a commit's change check runs before approval. Approving without a check makes these statements untrue for wording-only commits. The 'main' and 'approval' glossary entries also don't mention the exception.
findings.where: SKILL.md Authoring Purpose announcement; glossary 'change check'

findings.problem: The new example commit C3 (seq 3, content e5f6) reuses the id used by the Delivery example R2, 'commit 3-e5f6', which is a build with a failing harness. That makes the world fixtures ambiguous. C3 is an unchecked wording-only commit, while 3-e5f6 is treated elsewhere as a built commit whose harness failed.

The new wording_only flag on Commit can never be set. record_commit takes only seq, content, interface, domain, branch and author, and no other action sets wording_only. The bypass therefore cannot happen in practice. If it is set outside the declared actions, the flag is unverified and anyone who can set it skips the change check.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Commit object (wording_only) and record_commit params

findings.problem: The bypass condition is `checks_passed == true or wording_only == true`, so a wording_only commit whose change check was run and failed (checks_passed false, failing set) can still be approved and recorded as approved. This contradicts the intent that a check which has been run must pass. The rule is only meant to skip a check that has not been run.

The Authoring purpose announcement still promises 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed.' Wording-only commits are now approved with no change check, so that statement no longer holds. The change check also includes the stranded-objects check, which is skipped for these commits.

The glossary entry `approval` and the descriptions of `main` and `deliver` assume approved commits have passed the check. The `check_commit` and `record_check` preconditions and the `cite_evidence` description likewise treat checking as the route to approval. Approving a commit that has not been checked is now allowed, and these entries and the old check-then-approve flow are not updated to say so.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Authoring glossary (approval, main) and `deliver` precondition `approved`

findings.problem: The new example only covers a wording_only commit with checks_passed unset. No example covers wording_only together with checks_passed false, and none covers a commit without the flag. Neither the failed-check-plus-wording_only case nor the flag being wrongly set is tested.

The wording_only exemption also applies to a commit whose change check was run and failed. With `checks_passed == false` and `wording_only == true`, the `checks-pass` precondition, the `approved-only-if-checked` precondition and the invariant all let the approval through. This contradicts the retained rule that a failing commit is not approved, and a failed check should block approval.

No action can set Commit.wording_only. `record_commit` takes no such param, and no other action writes it. The flag is therefore either never true, so the feature does nothing, or it is set by some unspecified outside route. Nothing checks that the commit really only changes wording. Commits are also immutable, so the flag cannot be corrected after the fact. A commit marked wording_only skips the safety check entirely.

The new example starts from commit C3 (seq 3, content e5f6, wording_only true). The delivery examples already use commit `3-e5f6` as a different fixture (R2, built, harness failed). The new commit is not defined in the world fixture the examples say they start from, so the two may clash or the new commit may not exist.

The change check is described as the safety gate before delivery, covering harness, past actions and stranded objects. The deploy floor and the Purpose statement ('Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed') still assume every approved commit was checked. A wording-only commit is now approved with no check, so that promise no longer holds. The Purpose text and the main/approval glossary entries were not updated.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Authoring Purpose announcement; glossary `approval` and `main`

findings.problem: wording_only on Commit is a bare optional boolean that nothing sets. record_commit does not take it as a param, and no other action writes it. Nothing checks that a commit really changes only wording, and no actor restriction says who may mark it. The new example and rules therefore cannot be reached from a recorded commit, or else anyone could skip the change check by flagging a commit. Commit.wording_only has no verified source. No action sets it: record_commit takes no wording_only param, and the kernel's commit service does not compute it. A commit whose change check was run and failed (checks_passed false, with failing set) is still approvable and recordable as approved if wording_only is true.
